          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:142411631_1_3335'

Analysis Period

AWR snapshot range from 3334 to 3335.

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'NATRAJ' with DB ID 142411631.
Database version during analysis period was 19.29.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance natraj, numbered 1 and hosted at
natraj-db.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 38150 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 10.71.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                    Percent of Activity
   -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect   2.42 | 22.55         1
2  Soft Parse                       1.71 | 15.97         2
3  Top SQL Statements               1.2 | 11.19          3
4  Shared Pool Latches              .76 | 7.06           0

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 2.41 active sessions, 22.55% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 2.42 active sessions, 22.55% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.71 active sessions, 15.97% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.71 active sessions, 15.97% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.71 active sessions, 15.97% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 1.2 active sessions, 11.19% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .7 active sessions, 6.56% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 5% for SQL execution,
      38% for parsing, 57% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .28 active sessions, 2.57% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the UPDATE statement with SQL_ID
      "9zg9qd9bm4spu".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 9zg9qd9bm4spu.
         update user$ set spare6=DECODE(to_char(:2, 'YYYY-MM-DD'),
         '0000-00-00', to_date(NULL), :2) where user#=:1
   Rationale
      The SQL spent 100% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 100% for SQL
      execution, 0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "9zg9qd9bm4spu" was executed 289512 times and
      had an average elapsed time of 0.0028 seconds.

   Recommendation 3: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .22 active sessions, 2.06% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "1z6usjb6zxsty".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 1z6usjb6zxsty.

   Rationale
      The SQL spent 100% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 100% for SQL
      execution, 0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
   Rationale
      Top level calls to execute the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID
      "4brm7ybaxqq5v" are responsible for 100% of the database time spent on
      the INSERT statement with SQL_ID "1z6usjb6zxsty".
      Related Object

Finding 4: Shared Pool Latches
Impact is .76 active sessions, 7.06% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Contention for latches related to the shared pool was consuming significant
database time.
Waits for "library cache: mutex X" amounted to 1% of database time.
Waits for "latch: shared pool" amounted to 2% of database time.
Waits for "library cache: bucket mutex X" amounted to 2% of database time.

   No recommendations are available.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .8 active sessions, 7.46% of total activity.


Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .41 active sessions, 3.84% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .41 active sessions, 3.84% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .86 active sessions, 7.99% of total activity.


Finding 6: Undersized SGA
Impact is .22 active sessions, 2.04% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "102400 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .03 active sessions, .27% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      108800 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .86 active sessions, 7.99% of total activity.
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
